knowledge_gaps: The intervention requires unspecified backbone hooks. Correctness depends on the actual HSTU implementation, including fused attention, residual paths, relative biases and sequence-length scaling. Masking must prevent blocked content from reaching the readout through any layer while leaving default inference unchanged.

The protocol omits context-set sizes, eligibility rules, history truncation, candidate-sampling seeds, tie handling, margin definitions and bootstrap settings. Context blocking and bias ablation may interact, so separate ablations alone cannot fully distinguish their effects. The supplied backbone does not consume timestamps; temporal-bias probes should therefore be marked unavailable.

No prespecified rule connects diagnostic findings to a training change or measurable validation gain. In-sample sensitivity cannot substantiate the potential rating of 8/10, and code difficulty of 5/10 remains uncertain without backbone access. The recency citation also needs verification before supporting methodological choices.

follow_up_queries.reason: Establish implementable masking semantics and correctness tests before attributing effects to context access.
follow_up_queries.query: In HSTU (Actions Speak Louder than Words, arXiv:2402.17152) and its public reference implementation, how are causal validity masks, SiLU attention, relative positional bias, residual connections and sequence-length normalization applied? How can selected key/value contributions be blocked at every layer while preserving sequence slots and the final readout, and what tests establish zero dependence on blocked item embeddings and unchanged outputs under an empty intervention?

follow_up_queries.reason: Determine whether the proposed component separation needs interaction controls and a more explicit reproducible protocol.
follow_up_queries.query: What methodological guidance exists for factorial attention ablations in sequential recommenders, particularly HSTU, when comparing matched recent versus older context blocking with relative-position-bias removal? How should interaction effects, positional distance, context-set size, negative sampling, ranking ties and paired user-bootstrap uncertainty be handled when reporting sampled HR@10?

follow_up_queries.reason: Verify the supporting evidence and assess whether frozen-model sensitivity can justify a subsequent training experiment.
follow_up_queries.query: Does RecPO at https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.656/ actually provide evidence about interaction recency and preference intensity? What published evidence shows that frozen-model context-ablation sensitivity predicts benefits from context dropout or relative-bias regularization in sequential recommendation, and what validation design avoids selecting those changes from in-sample sensitivity alone?
